correctness.rationale: For each fixed p=1 mod3 and fixed B, Hensel lifting produces unit r mod p^B with r²+r+1=0. Dirichlet reciprocal-prime divergence for primes q≡r (mod p^B) plus CRT on the pairwise coprime q² cylinders gives density-one existence of q||m. Multiplicativity then forces p^B|sigma(m²) on density-one m. For any fixed T>=1 choose finite sets of p≡1 mod3 with p>T and B=2. Apart from a density-zero exceptional union, any p||m implies p|R(m), so R(m)<=T forces avoiding all those p||m; exact CRT upper-density <=product_p(1-1/p+1/p²). Let finite P exhaust p≡1 mod3; divergent reciprocal prime sum drives product to 0. Every quantifier is fixed before its limit. This proves bounded R has zero natural density and the R=1 equality conjecture. Independent exact prefix counts m<=1000 matched 10,99,974, roots mod49 are 18,30 and CRT avoidance q=7,13 is 6751/8281; no finite search used as the limit proof.

originality.rationale: Dris 2022 explicitly states zero density as Conjecture 5.1 after a bound below one; Meyerowitz 2020 gives the primitive-root mechanism with a heuristic infinite Euler product but leaves inter-prime justification. Finite CRT cylinder products with rigorously ordered limiting arguments establish it and also prove stronger divergence in density. Resultary prior supplies an asymptotically density-zero subfamily lower bound, logically compatible and not dominating.
residual_risks: The analytic density argument gives no quantitative rate or pointwise escape along all integer sequences.
